motivation: The bounded CPU replay showed identical initialization, full RNG state, forward attention boundaries, incoming output gradients, and predicted memory writes, but the shared scalar xmem_strength gradient differed slightly before clipping. The existing runner already enables deterministic PyTorch algorithms and single-threaded backward/reductions. The current implementation multiplies the same scalar separately into each query-chunk affinity score, creating many backward contributions to one scalar parameter.

change.only_change: Concatenate the existing query-chunk affinity scores, multiply the shared scalar strength once, then split the resulting bias back into the same query chunks for the same native scaled-dot-product-attention calls.
change.mathematics: The per-query, per-memory-token logit bias is unchanged: xmem_strength multiplied by the same XMem-style score. This only consolidates the shared scalar's autograd reduction.
